transitionDescOff: The old track stops and the new one starts at once.
transitionDescDip: The old track fades out, then the new one fades in from its beginning.
transitionDescCut: No fade: the new track starts exactly on the next cycle, on the beat.
transitionDescCrossfade: The new track comes in under the old one while the old one fades out.
transitionDescFilterSweep: Like a crossfade, but the old track thins out while the new one opens up.
transitionDescBassSwap: Both play together; halfway through, the bass moves from the old track to the new one.
transitionDescEchoOut: The old track dissolves into a fading echo while the new one starts.
transitionDescLayeredIntro: The new track's layers come in one by one while the old track fades out.
transitionGlideDescription: The tempo moves gradually from the old track's to the new one's
transitionMatchLoudnessDescription: The new track is brought to about the old track's loudness
transitionPicker: Transition for the next track switch
transitionWaiting: The switch is waiting for the next boundary
transitionNewTrackFailed: The new track has an error — the previous track keeps playing.
scratchDescription: Grab the record to scratch what is playing. Let go, and the track carries on, on the beat.
scratchPlatter: Scratch platter: drag to scratch, scroll to nudge
scratchPreviewOff: Headphones needs the headphone preview to be playing.
scratchNotPlaying: Nothing is playing on this deck.
scratchUnavailable: Scratching isn't available on this deck yet.
scratchShortcutHint: Hold Alt+Shift+← to pull back or Alt+Shift+→ to push forwards (not while typing in the editor).
scratchShortcutWindowsNote: On Windows, Alt+Shift may also switch the keyboard layout.
scratchMidiLearning: Turn the jog wheel on your controller…
scratchMidiLearnTimeout: No control was turned. Nothing changed.
scratchMidiUnsupported: This browser has no MIDI support. The platter still works.
scratchMidiDenied: MIDI access was denied. The platter still works.
scratchMidiError: MIDI could not be started. The platter still works.

equalizerSubtitle: 10-band parametric EQ with low/high cut and 81 presets
equalizerDragSliders: Drag sliders to adjust frequency bands
equalizerRecommendTurnsOn: Apply also turns the EQ on
equalizerWhyBrazilianFunk: The tamborzão kick and sub drive it; MC vocals and bright percussion sit on top.
equalizerWhyAutomotivo: A huge distorted car-sound sub, scooped low mids, and hard synth stabs on top.
equalizerWhyMontagem: Vocal chops over a heavy sub; scooped low mids and sharp high leads.
equalizerWhyFunkAgressivo: A big low end with a forward, biting upper mid for the aggression.
equalizerWhyMandelao: Raw, heavy São Paulo bass with the low mids cleared and a rolled-off top.
equalizerWhyBruxaria: Distorted sub and eerie chants; a presence lift for the screams, a darkened top.
equalizerWhyMandelaoSlowed: A sub that drags and heavy bass; the muffled top gives the slowed-down feel.
equalizerWhyFunkCariocaOldSchool: Miami-bass 808s and volt-mix drums; MC vocals forward, a soft vinyl top.
equalizerWhyBaileFunk: Tamborzão percussion and atabaque snap, with the kick and sub up front.
equalizerWhyReggaeton: The dembow kick and snare drive it: clean sub, vocals in front, crisp hats.
equalizerWhyDembow: Fast kick, cracking snare and hard synth stabs: bright and aggressive.
equalizerWhyCumbia: Güira scrape, accordion and bass lines live in the mids; no sub needed.
equalizerWhyAfroHouse: Deep kick and warm bass under tribal congas and shakers that need air.
equalizerWhyAmapiano: The log drum lives in the sub and bass; airy shakers and pads on top.
equalizerWhyPhonk: The 808 sub and cowbell carry the track; the high cut gives the lo-fi Memphis edge.
equalizerWhyDriftPhonk: The 808 sub and cowbell carry the track; the muffled top gives the tape-drift feel.
equalizerWhyTrap: Long 808 subs, room for vocals in the low mids, crisp hi-hat rolls on top.
equalizerWhyBrazilianPhonk: Distorted funk sub and cowbell melodies, pushed hard in the presence range.
equalizerWhyHousePhonk: Four-on-the-floor kick and bass, with cowbells cutting through the mix.
equalizerWhyMemphis: Tape-dubbed 808s and dark samples; the high cut gives the cassette feel.
equalizerWhyBoomBap: Kick and snare punch over warm samples, a little vinyl dullness on top.
equalizerWhyLofiHipHop: Soft, warm and dusty; the highs are rolled off for a relaxed, worn-tape sound.
equalizerWhyUkDrill: Sliding 808 sub, dark scooped low mids, sharp hi-hat patterns on top.
equalizerWhyNyDrill: Harder than UK drill: distorted 808 slides and punchier drums.
equalizerWhyRage: Blown-out 808s and distorted synth leads: loud, bright and wide open.
equalizerWhyPlugg: Soft, round 808s and sparkly bell melodies; the mids stay out of the way.
equalizerWhyCloudRap: Hazy pads over a deep sub; the air band carries the dreamy reverb.
equalizerWhyJerseyClub: Kick triplets, bed-squeak samples and vocal chops that need snap.
equalizerWhyElectro: A punchy 808 kick, snappy claps and bright synths.
equalizerWhyTechno: Kick punch at 60–125 Hz, darker mids, crisp hats; the rumble is cut.
equalizerWhyDrumAndBass: A clean sub with the rumble cut, scooped low mids, snare snap and air.
equalizerWhyDubstep: A massive sub, growling mid bass and a cracking snare.
equalizerWhyHouse: A steady kick and warm bassline; open hats with a little shine.
equalizerWhyDeepHouse: Round, warm bass and soft chords; the top stays smooth.
equalizerWhyTechHouse: A tight, punchy kick, a rolling bass groove and crisp percussion.
equalizerWhyMinimal: Small, precise sounds: a light lift on the kick and the clicks.
equalizerWhyHardTechno: A pounding, distorted kick at 60–125 Hz and industrial percussion.
equalizerWhyTrance: A driving bass and wide supersaw leads that need air on top.
equalizerWhyPsytrance: The rolling bassline sits at 60–125 Hz under squelchy, psychedelic highs.
equalizerWhyHardstyle: The distorted kick punches at 60–120 Hz; harsh, screeching mids on top.
equalizerWhyGabber: A brutally distorted kick from the sub into the low mids, harsh and raw.
equalizerWhyUkGarage: Shuffled hats in the air band and a warm sub under swung beats.
equalizerWhyJungle: Deep sub bass under chopped breakbeats with cracking snares.
equalizerWhyBreakbeat: Punchy breaks: a solid kick and the snare's crack in the presence range.
equalizerWhySynthwave: Warm analog synths and gated snares, with a slightly soft retro top.
equalizerWhyHyperpop: Maximal and bright: pitched vocals, distorted bass and lots of air.
equalizerWhyFutureBass: Sidechained supersaw chords over a deep sub, with sparkly highs.
equalizerWhyRiddim: A heavy sub and repetitive, metallic mid-bass wobbles.
equalizerWhyRockGenre: Guitars and vocals in the presence range, a punchy kick, no rumble.
equalizerWhyMetal: Scooped mids, a tight kick and an aggressive guitar presence.
equalizerWhyPunk: Raw, mid-forward guitars and snare; a lean low end, nothing polished.
equalizerWhyUsFunk: Slap bass and tight drums; horns and guitar chops in the upper mids.
equalizerWhyDisco: Four-on-the-floor kick and octave bass; strings and open hats with shine.
equalizerWhySoul: Warm vocals and an analog band: full low mids and a gentle top.
equalizerWhyReggae: Deep bass and one-drop drums lead; the highs are rolled off and warm.
equalizerWhyDub: The bass is everything; the echoes sit low and the top is rolled off.
equalizerWhyAmbient: Gentle and wide: small changes, so long textures stay natural.
equalizerWhyChillout: A soft, warm low end and a smooth, relaxed top.
equalizerWhyLofi: Tape and cassette character: the low and high cuts narrow the band.
